neighbours.label: prestige and reach descriptors in university promotional prose (international, global, exceptional, highly ranked)
fire: Founded in 1890, the college is an internationally renowned centre for medical research.
Our graduates join a global network of alumni in over 100 countries.
As a highly ranked public university, we welcome students from every state.
The faculty enjoys an international reputation for teaching excellence.
Students gain exceptional access to labs, museums and leading scholars.
A world-class research university with campuses in Europe and Asia.
The school's global reach gives undergraduates study options abroad.
Few institutions offer such internationally recognized degree programs.
quiet: Founded in 1890, the bakery is known for its rye bread.
The company has a global network of suppliers in over 100 countries.
The highly ranked tennis player lost in the first round.
The airline has an international route to Lisbon twice a week.
Visitors have easy access to the beach from the hotel.
The college library closes at ten on weekdays.
Global sales of the phone fell in the last quarter.
The dormitory has two washing machines on each floor.

predictions: Prestige descriptors in university blurbs fire; the same descriptors in business or news text, and plain campus facts, stay quiet.
notes: Probe: 'international reach of our seven schools' 0.711, 'internationally recognized research university' 0.497, 'exceptional access' 0.435, 'A global university' 0.229; 'international shipping' 0.067, 'global economy' 0.040, cafeteria 0.013.
